CLAUDE.md — HowMaHiCo

Source: CLAUDE.md

What this is

An LC-immunopeptidomics (MHC/HLA peptide) data-analysis project: a parameterized RMarkdown reporting pipeline that ingests LC-MS search-engine output (FragPipe, DIA-NN, PEAKS), normalizes it into one unified long-format table (pep_all), and renders self-contained interactive HTML QC reports plus csv/xlsx/png result exports.

Current version: 0.17.0 — Phases 1–6 of the package conversion are complete. v0.17.0 is a distributability pass: the report header attribution is no longer hardcoded. Every skeleton branded its output to one platform (“provided by the Immunopeptidomics Platform (IPP)”, plus a personal @dkfz.de address and a **Code author:** DGZ line in the two 00_* reports); all nine templates now declare an optional Provider param and render the line through the new exported provider_line() (R/report-helpers.R), which falls back to a generic sentence naming no organisation when Provider is empty. Called namespaced (`r HowMaHiCo::provider_line(params$Provider)`) because in the two 00_* templates the header sits above their inline setup chunk, so the package is not attached yet. Also new: inst/scripts/howmahico_pipeline.R + the exported get_pipeline_script() (a sibling of get_report_template() / get_dictionary_template()) — a runnable, commented walkthrough that renders via run_howmahico_report() rather than by opening a template, and that starts in a demo mode running end-to-end against inst/extdata/sim_fragpipe_dda with no user data; and the package’s first vignette (vignettes/howmahico.Rmd, VignetteBuilder: knitr), which gives the pkgdown site an Articles tab. The README was corrected and expanded — its headline example passed a Title param no template declares, and rmarkdown errors on undeclared params, so the primary documented entry point failed on copy-paste. v0.16.1 fixed the pkgdown site build, which had failed on every master push since v0.8.0: pkgdown aborts when an exported function is missing from the _pkgdown.yml reference index, and v0.9.0–v0.13.0 added 15 exports without indexing them. devtools::check() never reads _pkgdown.yml and the pkgdown workflow only runs on master, so the break was only visible after a merge — tests/testthat/test-pkgdown-index.R now guards it in the ordinary suite (exports ⊆ index, no stale entries, no duplicates; it walks up to find the .Rbuildignored _pkgdown.yml and skips when no source tree is reachable). v0.16.0 added the peptide-chemistry report 07_pepchem and its engine R/pepchem.R — the first part of HowMaHiCo that describes what the ligands are made of rather than which they are. pepchem_by_sample() reduces pep_all to its distinct Sequence per Sample and attaches the descriptors from peptide_properties() (GRAVY, pI, Charge, MW, Boman, HydrophobicMoment, InstabilityIndex, AliphaticIndex + frac_* amino-acid class fractions), computed once over the unique sequences; aa_composition() and aa_position_frequency() give the position-independent and per-position residue tables (the latter generalises anchor_information_content(), and the two now share .aa_alphabet() / .resolve_positions()). The unit of analysis is the sample, not the peptide: summarise_pepchem() collapses each sample to one value per descriptor, aggregate_pepchem() gives the per-Condition mean ± sd across samples, and compare_pepchem(level = "sample") tests across samples (Kruskal-Wallis + pairwise Wilcoxon, BH within a contrast, MedianDiff + the new scale-free cliffs_delta()). That test is deliberately low-powered — on 3 vs 3 samples a two-sided Wilcoxon cannot reach p < 0.1, the same structural limit 06_quant_stats documents for its Fisher track — so level = "peptide" is reported alongside as an explicitly pseudo-replicated, descriptive track. compare_aa_frequency() applies the same machinery per residue to per-sample frequencies (not a chi-square on pooled residue counts, which would treat every residue as an independent draw). New plots in R/plots.R: plot_aa_composition() (bar / heatmap / log2 enrichment vs. the pooled composition), plot_aa_position_heatmap(), plot_property_distribution(), plot_property_sample_summary(), plot_property_effectsize(). New dependency Peptides (CRAN, GPL-2, Rcpp only) in Imports — vectorised and the canonical GRAVY implementation, so the scales are not re-derived; Peptides::aaComp() is not used (per-sequence list) and its per-descriptor “unrecognized amino acid types” warnings are consolidated into one. Peptide position within the parent protein was deferred — see Deferred designs below. Two silent-failure fixes found while verifying it: (a) ggsave_rawr() / ggprint_rawr() resolved the plot name with a bare exists(), which searches from the helper’s own frame outwards (namespace → globalenv()) and never reaches a report’s knit env (new.env(parent = globalenv())) — so PlotsSave = TRUE wrote no png in any report and ggprint_rawr() returned the warning string instead of the plot, swallowed by warning = FALSE chunks. The name is now resolved in the caller’s frame via the shared internal .plot_was_built() (R/theme-and-save.R), and a non-symbol argument (plots[[nm]], the export-loop idiom) is judged by value so a NULL plot is skipped; (b) 05_quality_score had never rendered — an inline `r ...` expression ended in a bare comma-separated string list instead of a paste0() call, a syntax error caught only at inline-parse time, and no test rendered that template. Both are guarded by new tests. v0.15.0 was a robustness + schema pass driven by plans_dgz.md. Mouse MHC-I: MHCclass accepts "MHC1_mouse" (7–11 AAs) next to MHC1 (8–13) and MHC2 (12–25); the windows/palettes now come from mhc_length_window() / mhc_class_palette() in the new R/report-helpers.R instead of three copy-pasted lists in the skeletons plus a fourth inside .cross_class_range(). The quality score follows: for mouse, frac_9mer counts 8- and 9-mers (H-2Kb favours 8-mers, H-2Db 9-mers) with the label “8/9-mer fraction” and higher cut-offs (quality_thresholds_default() gained an mhcclass arg), and the anchor motif is scored on whichever of the two lengths dominates — metric keys unchanged. Three abort/silent-failure fixes: (a) a single-Condition subset no longer kills every report — combn(conditions, 2) is replaced by the exported condition_pairs() (empty list for one Condition, self = TRUE for the overlap matrix diagonal); (b) an all-zero-Area dataset no longer aborts — get_mat_log2area() returns a 0 x n matrix with a warning and the correlation chunks test for it before cor() (which errors with 'x' is empty); (c) get_annot_sampleid() warns when nothing/only some of the annotation matched the HyStar sample list and gained keep_all = TRUE (left join). TestMode rebuilt: files are read in full and reduced to ~100 rows per run (subsample_testmode() in R/utils-loaders.R) instead of the first 100 lines of the file — for a combined FragPipe psm.tsv the old behaviour kept only the first run and broke the annotation join. One annotation format for every engine: read_annot() accepts a canonical Sample_folder column and derives Sample_fp (verbatim) and Sample_peaks (PEAKS-normalized) from it, so the loaders are untouched and legacy CSVs still load; get_annot_fragpipe()/get_annot_diann() emit Sample_folder, and PEAKS gained get_annot_peaks(). v0.14.0 added the advanced-quantification report 06_quant_stats and its engine R/quant-stats.R — the first part of HowMaHiCo that compares conditions rather than describing them. build_quant_matrix() collapses pep_all into a feature × unit log2 matrix (Area summed over precursors on the linear scale, technical replicates averaged into their BioReplicate), then filter_quant() → normalize_quant() → impute_quant() → test_differential() (limma ~ 0 + Condition with pairwise contrasts and eBayes(trend = TRUE, robust = TRUE), or a dependency-free Welch "ttest") → test_detection() (Fisher exact on detection counts) → combine_quant_results() / summarise_significant(), plus permanova_condition() (base-R Anderson-2001 pseudo-F permutation test). Missing values run on two tracks: the quantitative test on observed (or imputed) values, and a presence/absence track for condition-exclusive ligands whose fold change is undefined — flagged by a detection-count rule, not an FDR cut-off, because a 3-vs-3 Fisher test cannot go below p = 0.1. limma is a Suggests dependency, guarded by the internal .require_limma(); the report falls back to StatMethod = "ttest" / NormMethod = "median" automatically when it is absent. New plots in R/plots.R: plot_completeness(), plot_missing_heatmap(), plot_intensity_dist(), plot_dynamic_range(), plot_pca(), plot_quant_heatmap() (clustered/unclustered ggplot2 tile map — plot_heatmap() writes a png and cannot be printed in a tabset), plot_volcano(), plot_ma(), plot_pvalue_hist(), plot_sig_summary(). The report carries its own “Methods & justification” section. Also fixed: run_howmahico_report("05_quality_score") was unreachable (documented but absent from the match.arg choices) — 05 and 06 are now registered and test-report-templates.R guards that every shipped template directory is offered. v0.13.0 was a plots/exports pass driven by plans_dgz.md: plot_pseudochromatogram() now fills RT bars by peptide count (density gradient) instead of per-Condition colour; new plot_pseudomobilogram() (count vs invk0, configurable binwidth, default 0.2) was added next to it and wired into 03_lcms_qc (new “Pseudomobilograms” tab in the RT/1k0/mz view config) and 00_mhc_report; plot_charge_proportions() bars gained a black outline; the peptide-motif window was extended to 7–25 AAs (01_id_counts/00_mhc_report, was capped at 24); and a subset prefix is now applied to every result filename via a shared result_prefix (= Subset, NULL when unset) passed to write.csv_rawr() / write_input_params() and the seq_by_condition.xlsx write (e.g. dda_all_pep_all.csv; input_params combines subset + report name to avoid collisions). The “implement safeguard when some conditions/replicates give 0 areas” item was moved to standby (no repro). v0.12.0 was a focused-report polish pass (no new engines): 01_id_counts gained an Average +/- sd per BioReplicate section mirroring the per-Condition one (plot_count_mean_sd() gained a group_var arg, default "Condition"); its Proportion by length content was pulled into its own 2nd-level section with Condition / BioReplicate / Sample tabs (previously nested under the Total-by sections). 02_overlaps gained an Overlap intra-Condition (%) section (plot_overlap_intra_condition() gained a value arg, "count"/"percent"). Across the focused templates, “Selected peptides” headers now show the active length window (e.g. “(8 to 13 AAs)”) via shortpep_range, and the “Proteins” ID-level headers/labels were renamed to “Parent proteins” — display only: the data keys (counts_levels, n_Proteins columns, count_lim$Level) and plot axis labels are unchanged (a separate counts_labels display vector backs the renamed headers). The InteractivePlots/ggplotly toggle remains on the to-do list. v0.11.0 added a cross-class (MHC1↔︎MHC2) contamination dimension to the quality score: frac_cross_class flags MHC-II ligands co-enriched in an MHC-I pulldown (and vice versa) by their length signature — the fraction of peptides in the other class’s canonical window (MHC1 8–13, MHC2 12–25) that falls outside the current window (the internal .cross_class_range() is the single source of truth; the “outside-current” qualifier handles the 12–13 AA overlap). Scored lower_better at low weight (a small tail is biologically normal), NA/dropped for custom length windows. New plot plot_cross_class_length() (per-sample length histogram with the cross-class region highlighted) + a “Cross-class contamination” section in the 05_quality_score report. v0.10.0 added a per-sample immunopeptidomics quality score (inspired by the author’s HowDirty contamination score, but inverted — it scores how strongly a sample resembles a real HLA immunopeptidome). New engine R/quality-score.R exports score_sample_quality() (per-sample composite 0–100 + traffic-light category), qc_metrics_by_sample() (raw signals: length-window fidelity, 9-mer dominance, anchor-motif clarity via anchor_information_content(), non-tryptic specificity, charge plausibility, depth, mass accuracy — all from pep_all, no external data, no new dependency), score_curve(), quality_thresholds_default(), calibrate_thresholds_from_qc(); plus plot_quality_heatmap() / plot_quality_composite() in R/plots.R. The non-tryptic signal is split: overall C-terminal K/R fraction is a low-weight diagnostic (some HLA-I alleles use K/R anchors), while the scored metric isolates tryptic background in the out-of-window long-peptide tail. Thresholds use literature defaults or are calibrated from samples tagged as QC controls via an optional annotation QC column (ThresholdMode = "qc_relative"); undefined dimensions (MHC-II anchors, DIA-NN dummy ppm) drop out of the weighted composite instead of penalising the sample. New focused report 05_quality_score (inst/rmarkdown/templates/05_quality_score/) renders the score against the cached pep_all like the other focused reports. tests/testthat/test-quality-score.R covers score_curve() / anchor_information_content() (pure math, no synthetic peptide data). v0.9.0 added a dictionary-driven unified parser so a tabular search-engine export from a tool with no built-in loader can be ingested by editing a YAML dictionary (no R coding, no new loader). New build_pep_all() branch software = "custom" (with a dictionary arg) runs read_custom_batch() → parse_unified() → annotate_unified(). The dictionary maps raw→pep_all columns, sets the Found_By constant, and derives the shared recipe (Log2Area, Length_range, Nter/Cter, PeptideID, Charge formatting); per-tool transforms (unit conversions, regex extraction, accession splitting) are pre-clean responsibilities, not dictionary-expressible. New exports: read_dictionary(), parse_unified() (R/parse-unified.R), read_custom_batch(), annotate_unified() (R/loaders-custom.R), get_dictionary_template() (R/get-dictionary.R). Reference dictionaries ship in inst/extdata/dictionaries/ (custom_template.yaml + fragpipe.yaml / diann.yaml / peaks.yaml); the three built-in loaders are unchanged. tests/testthat/test-parse-unified.R round-trips parse_unified() against the FragPipe loader. New dependency: yaml (transitive via rmarkdown). Custom software has no inline-parsing path in the two 00_* reports — run build_pep_all("custom", dictionary=...) once, then render the focused reports with PepAllSource = "cached". v0.8.0 gave the four focused reports a PepAllSource param ("cached" | "rda" | "build", via inst/rmarkdown/shared/setup.Rmd) so each can load the default cache, load an explicit .rda (PepAllFile), or self-build from raw results via build_pep_all(); and added a simulated FragPipe dataset (inst/extdata/sim_fragpipe_dda/, moved out of data/) with tests/testthat/test-sim-fragpipe.R (a build_pep_all assertion + the first end-to-end render test of a focused report). v0.7.1 fixed a “Duplicate chunk label ‘setup’” parse error that aborted all four focused reports: the shared inst/rmarkdown/shared/setup.Rmd had a fenced r-chunk example inside its leading HTML comment, and knitr parses chunk headers even inside comments (re-including the file → duplicate setup). Comment is now prose; tests/testthat/test-report-templates.R guards against it. v0.7.0 renumbered all report templates (breaking: the template= names change): 01_mhc_report→00_mhc_report, 02_mhc_upsets→00_mhc_upsets, 03_id_counts→01_id_counts, 04_overlaps→02_overlaps, 05_lcms_qc→03_lcms_qc, 06_quant→04_quant; and rewrote the LC-MS report’s RT/1k0/m_z section to a single looped results='asis' chunk (config list of views × peptide sets) instead of eight hand-written chunks. The multi-report framework (v0.6.0): a new exported build_pep_all() (R/build-pep-all.R) extracts the raw-file parse/cache step, and the four focused templates each render a slice of the all-in-one 00_mhc_report against the cached pep_all (loaded via the shared inst/rmarkdown/shared/setup.Rmd knitr child). Build the cache once, then render any subset. 00_mhc_report/00_mhc_upsets are the all-in-one reports (parse the raw files themselves); v0.6.1 moved the PTM profile into 01_id_counts with an all-peptides variant. v0.5.0 split two report sections by length to match the “Average +/- sd” pattern: plot_overlap_intra_condition() is now a single-plot function (breaking signature: (df, id_col, title, shortpep_range) — was (pep_all, pep_short, id_col, ...)), and the “Overlap intra-Condition” + “Peptides identified per charge” report sections now show All peptides / Selected peptides (pep_short) as separate nested tabsets. v0.4.0 was a loader-consistency + report-robustness pass: the three loaders now share compute_log2area() (zero Area → NA everywhere, previously 1 for FragPipe/DIA-NN and NA for PEAKS — a user-visible behavior change), extract_run_name() (POSIX-safe run-name extraction, no longer Windows-backslash-only), and validate_pep_all() (core-schema guard at each parser tail) — all internal helpers in R/utils-loaders.R. The 00_mhc_report template (then named 01_mhc_report) degrades gracefully on partial subsets (single-Condition UpSets, no-replicate Area %CV), both all-in-one templates gained a “Session & provenance” footer, and 00_mhc_upsets now declares its DataAcquisitionNames param. v0.3.0 was a best-practices pass: base-package imports declared, all exports made public (no @keywords internal), NEWS.md added, internal code unified on the native |> pipe (R floor raised to 4.1.0). project-style-guide.md documents the target R-package + Docker + Shiny distribution pattern. The package layout is authoritative — DESCRIPTION, LICENSE/LICENSE.md, NAMESPACE, R/ (100+ exported functions plus the report entry point), inst/rmarkdown/templates/ (the two Rmd report templates), tests/testthat/ (hand-synthesized fixtures + a full testthat-edition-3 suite — loaders, annotation, checks, counting, io-export, overlap-counters, plotting smoke tests), .github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml (Win+Ubuntu CI, green), man/, _pkgdown.yml, .Rbuildignore — library(HowMaHiCo) (or devtools::load_all()) gives you everything. devtools::check() is clean (0 errors/0 warnings). Docker/Shiny/.bat distribution tiers remain (Phases 7–9). The original 0_code/-based files have been moved to example/ (gitignored) as pre-migration reference copies — no longer canonical. RStudio project file: HowMaHiCo.Rproj. Tracked in a private GitHub repo (DavidGZ1/HowMaHiCo, remote origin); 2_data/, 3_results/, 4_figures/, example/, and rendered *.html reports are gitignored.

R/loaders-peaks-dirs.R holds get_dirs_index_peaks(), the internal helper that indexes PEAKS export subfolders for read_peaks_batch(). It was originally adapted from the author’s other package deltaProtR (github.com/DavidGZ1/deltaProtR) but is now native HowMaHiCo code — deltaProtR is not a dependency (no Imports/Remotes: entry anywhere: CI/Docker/installs).

Directory layout (numbered-folder convention)

Folder Contents
R/ Package source: all exported functions (100+) + internal helpers
inst/rmarkdown/templates/ 00_mhc_report/, 00_mhc_upsets/, and the focused 01_id_counts/, 02_overlaps/, 03_lcms_qc/, 04_quant/, 05_quality_score/, 06_quant_stats/, 07_pepchem/ skeleton Rmds (+ shared inst/rmarkdown/shared/setup.Rmd)
inst/scripts/ howmahico_pipeline.R — the guided, runnable walkthrough handed out by get_pipeline_script()
vignettes/ howmahico.Rmd — the narrated walkthrough (vignette("howmahico"))
inst/extdata/dictionaries/ YAML parser dictionaries for the software = "custom" path: custom_template.yaml (fill-in) + fragpipe.yaml/diann.yaml/peaks.yaml (reference)
tests/testthat/ testthat-edition-3 test suite + hand-synthesized fixtures
man/ Roxygen-generated Rd files
example/ Legacy 0_code/, 1_documentation/ pre-migration reference copies (gitignored)
2_data/ Raw search-engine output (FragPipe psm.tsv, DIA-NN report.tsv) + cached *_pep_all.rda (gitignored)
3_results/<subset>/ Per-subset csv + xlsx outputs (pep_all.csv, counts_pep_all_condition.csv, seq_by_condition.xlsx, …) (gitignored)
4_figures/ Optional PNG plot exports (only when PlotsSave = TRUE) (gitignored)

Pipeline / data flow

LC-MS search output (FragPipe psm.tsv, DIA-NN report.tsv, PEAKS peptide.csv)
      │   read + parse + annotate  (software-specific loaders converge on one schema,
      │   exported from the HowMaHiCo package — library(HowMaHiCo))
      ▼
pep_all  — unified long-format table, cached as <FolderData>/<subset>_pep_all.rda
      │
      ▼
inst/rmarkdown/templates/00_mhc_report/skeleton/skeleton.Rmd
      │   rendered via run_howmahico_report() → self-contained interactive HTML report
      │   (ID counts, overlaps, distributions, QC sections — see below)
      ▼
<FolderResults>/<subset>/*.csv, *.xlsx, input_params.csv
      +   <FolderFigures>/<subset>/*.png (optional)

00_mhc_upsets (inst/rmarkdown/templates/00_mhc_upsets/) is the secondary overlap/UpSet-only report template, rendered the same way with template = "00_mhc_upsets". The focused reports (01_id_counts, 02_overlaps, 03_lcms_qc, 04_quant) each render one slice of 00_mhc_report against the cached pep_all (load it via build_pep_all() first); see the v0.6.0 framework note above.

Key files

  • R/loaders-fragpipe.R, R/loaders-diann.R, R/loaders-peaks.R — software-specific loader families converging on the pep_all schema:
    • read_fragpipe_batch / parse_fragpipe / annotate_fragpipe — FragPipe psm.tsv
    • read_diann_batch / parse_diann / annotate_diann — DIA-NN report.tsv
    • read_peaks_batch / read_peaks — PEAKS peptide.csv
    • Batch readers accept annotation = annot to read only files listed in the annotation table (3-way dispatch: explicit files > annotation table > scan folder)
  • R/annotation.R — read_annot, print_annot, get_annot_fragpipe, get_annot_diann, get_annot_sampleid
  • R/checks.R — check_file_exists, check_output_exists, check_ids_global
  • R/counting.R, R/overlap-counters.R — count_ids, count_ids_condition_bylengthrange, count_ids_by, get_charge_group, get_proportion_charge, get_mat_log2area, summarise_area, list_sequences, count_intersect, count_merged, count_samples_patients, select_unique, filter_unique
  • R/plots.R — plot_peplength_dens, plot_pepmass, plot_pepmz, plot_bp_count_length, plot_upset, plot_upset_batch, ggseqlogo_bylength, plot_prop_length_condition, plot_charge_proportions, plot_violin_areacv, plot_corr, theme_rawr, ggsave_rawr, ggprint_rawr
  • R/io.R — write.csv_rawr, write_input_params
  • R/run-report.R — run_howmahico_report, derive_filtered_annotation
  • R/get-report.R — get_report_template (copies a skeleton to the working dir)
  • R/parse-unified.R — read_dictionary() + parse_unified(): the dictionary-driven parser for the software = "custom" path (rename + Found_By + shared derived recipe + validate_pep_all guard)
  • R/loaders-custom.R — read_custom_batch() (generic configurable per-sample reader) + annotate_unified() (generic annotation join)
  • R/get-dictionary.R — get_dictionary_template (copies the YAML dictionary template to the working dir)
  • R/get-pipeline-script.R — get_pipeline_script (copies inst/scripts/howmahico_pipeline.R to the working dir; same system.file() → exists-guard → file.copy() shape as get_dictionary_template)
  • R/quality-score.R — the immunopeptidomics quality-score engine: qc_metrics_by_sample(), anchor_information_content(), score_curve(), quality_thresholds_default(), calibrate_thresholds_from_qc(), score_sample_quality() plus the internal .cross_class_range() (MHC1↔︎MHC2 cross-class window) feeding the frac_cross_class metric (consumed by the 05_quality_score report; plot_quality_heatmap()/plot_quality_composite()/plot_cross_class_length() live in R/plots.R)
  • R/quant-stats.R — the advanced-quantification engine behind 06_quant_stats: build_quant_matrix(), filter_quant(), normalize_quant(), impute_quant(), test_differential(), test_detection(), combine_quant_results(), summarise_significant(), permanova_condition() plus the internal .require_limma() / .pairwise_contrasts(). limma is a Suggests dependency; the method = "ttest" / NormMethod = "median" path needs no Bioconductor package. Its plots (plot_completeness(), plot_missing_heatmap(), plot_intensity_dist(), plot_dynamic_range(), plot_pca(), plot_quant_heatmap(), plot_volcano(), plot_ma(), plot_pvalue_hist(), plot_sig_summary()) live in R/plots.R
  • R/pepchem.R — the peptide-chemistry engine behind 07_pepchem: peptide_properties() (per-unique-sequence descriptors via Peptides), pepchem_properties() (the core/extended PropertySet lists), aa_composition(), aa_position_frequency() (per-position residue table; negative positions count from the C-terminus), pepchem_by_sample(), summarise_pepchem() → aggregate_pepchem() (the two-step per-sample → per-Condition aggregation), cliffs_delta(), compare_pepchem() and compare_aa_frequency(), plus the internal .aa_alphabet() / .resolve_positions() (shared with anchor_information_content()), .aa_classes(), .residue_counts() and the .compare_groups() test scaffold. Its plots (plot_aa_composition(), plot_aa_position_heatmap(), plot_property_distribution(), plot_property_sample_summary(), plot_property_effectsize()) live in R/plots.R
  • R/report-helpers.R — the settings the templates derive from their params: mhc_length_window() (MHC1 8–13 / MHC1_mouse 7–11 / MHC2 12–25, else the ShortPeptideLength* params), mhc_class_palette(), mhc_classes() and condition_pairs() (all pairwise Condition comparisons; empty list for a single Condition, self = TRUE adds the diagonal). Single source of truth — the skeletons and R/quality-score.R/R/quant-stats.R all call these
  • R/loaders-peaks-dirs.R — get_dirs_index_peaks(), the internal PEAKS export-subfolder indexer used by read_peaks_batch() (originally adapted from deltaProtR, now native)
  • inst/rmarkdown/templates/00_mhc_report/skeleton/skeleton.Rmd (~1100 lines) — the main QC report. Sections: total IDs (incl. decoys/contaminants) → ID counts (mean±sd, by length, by charge) → intra-condition replicate overlap → cross-condition UpSet plots → pairwise overlap matrices → peptide size distribution (length/mass/m_z) → 2D ID distributions (RT × 1/k0 × m/z, “pseudochromatograms”) → log2(Area) Pearson correlation → Area %CV violin plots → identification QC (Score, ppm by condition & charge) → peptide motifs (seqlogo by length) → PTM profile → export block
  • inst/rmarkdown/templates/00_mhc_upsets/skeleton/skeleton.Rmd — secondary report focused on overlap/UpSet plots (loads from cached .rda, same params)
  • inst/rmarkdown/templates/{01_id_counts,02_overlaps,03_lcms_qc,04_quant,05_quality_score,06_quant_stats,07_pepchem}/ — the focused reports (01–04 each a slice of 00_mhc_report; 05_quality_score is the per-sample quality-score report from R/quality-score.R; 06_quant_stats is the advanced-quantification / differential-abundance report from R/quant-stats.R; 07_pepchem is the peptide-physicochemical-properties report from R/pepchem.R), sharing inst/rmarkdown/shared/setup.Rmd and loading the pep_all cache from build_pep_all() (R/build-pep-all.R)

Annotation file schema (1_documentation/sample_annotation_*.csv)

Required columns (checked by read_annot): - Condition, BioReplicate, TechReplicate, Sample — always required - Sample_folder — the data subfolder name (e.g. fragpipe_dda_combined/JY), the same column whatever the search engine. The engine-specific legacy names Sample_fp (FragPipe/DIA-NN) and Sample_peaks (PEAKS) are still accepted; at least one of the three is required. read_annot() derives the missing ones: Sample_fp is a verbatim copy of Sample_folder, Sample_peaks a copy with PEAKS’ hyphen/space normalization — so the loaders, which key on Sample_fp/Sample_peaks, are unchanged. A user-supplied alias is never overwritten - Source_file — required when mode = "combined_file" (FragPipe combined PSM, DIA-NN); matches the spectrum/run name within that subfolder - Sample_ID — free-text human-readable identifier - QC (optional) — flags experiment quality-control samples (TRUE/"QC"); consumed by the 05_quality_score report to mark QC samples and, with ThresholdMode = "qc_relative", to calibrate the score thresholds. read_annot passes it through untouched (no schema change needed)

get_annot_fragpipe() / get_annot_diann() / get_annot_peaks() generate the skeleton table (with Sample_folder) for their respective exports.

Matching key for joining annotation ↔︎ data: Sample_fp alone for fragpipe_dda_individual; Sample_fp + Source_file for combined_file mode and DIA-NN. read_annot also strips .d/.raw extensions from Source_file and replaces hyphens/spaces in Sample_peaks with underscores (matching PEAKS’ own export behavior). Factor order for all downstream plots/tables is taken from row order in the CSV (mutate(across(where(is.character), function(x) factor(x, levels = unique(x))))).

The pep_all schema

The unified long-format table every report section consumes (one row per peptide-sample observation). Core columns: Condition, BioReplicate, TechReplicate, Sample, Sample_ID, Accession/ProteinFirst/GeneFirst/ OrganismFirst, Peptide/Sequence/Length/Length_range, Score, Area/Log2Area, PTM, Charge/Nter/Cter, RT/invk0/Mass/ppm/m_z, Source_file/Source_File_ID/Precursor_Id, Found_By, PeptideID. pep_short is the subset filtered to Length within [ShortPeptideLengthMin, ShortPeptideLengthMax] (8–13 AAs for HLA-I, the biologically expected MHC-I ligand length window).

pep_all is cached to 2_data/<Subset>_pep_all.rda (or pep_all.rda when Subset is empty) so subsequent runs/inspection don’t require re-parsing the raw search files.

How to run

Render reports with library(HowMaHiCo) + run_howmahico_report() — a thin wrapper around rmarkdown::render() that locates the installed package’s report template via system.file() and knits it in a fresh environment (avoids a params-argument / rmarkdown::render()-injected-params name collision; see R/run-report.R). One call renders one report (composable — loop it for batch runs; Docker-idiomatic “one container run = one job”):

library(HowMaHiCo)

# Step 1 — auto-generate annotation skeleton, then open and fill in metadata columns
get_annot_fragpipe(dir_data = "2_data") |>
  get_annot_sampleid(file_sample_list = "1_documentation/sample_list.xlsx") |>
  write.csv(row.names = FALSE, file = "1_documentation/sample_annotation_dda_all.csv")
# → open CSV, complete Condition / BioReplicate / TechReplicate / Sample_ID, save

# Step 2 — render (title is auto-generated from SampleSet / Subset / MHCclass / date)
run_howmahico_report(
  template = "00_mhc_report",            # or "00_mhc_upsets"
  params = list(SampleSet = "MEGF_035",
                AnnotationFile = "sample_annotation_dda_all.csv",
                FolderDocumentation = "1_documentation",
                Subset = "dda_all",
                FolderData = "2_data", FolderResults = "3_results", FolderFigures = "4_figures",
                Software = "fragpipe_dda_combined",
                MHCclass = "MHC1"),       # or "MHC2" for 12-25 AA window
  output_file = "01_report_main__hla1_dda_all.html"
)

The 6-subset batch pattern that 0_code/00_knit_reports.R used to drive directly — deriving the _jy/_plasma annotation CSVs, then looping render() over {dda,dia} × {all,jy,plasma} — is preserved as a \dontrun{} example on run_howmahico_report/derive_filtered_annotation (R/run-report.R); the latter is the exported helper for the annotation-derivation preprocessing step (derive_filtered_annotation("sample_annotation_dda_all.csv", "1_documentation", "JY")).

Breaking change from the 0_code/-era reports — path params are now absolute (or relative to the render-time working directory; no longer assumed project-root-relative, since the template ships inside an installed package and can be rendered from anywhere). There’s also a new param, FolderDocumentation, that the legacy Rmds didn’t need (they hardcoded 1_documentation/):

Param Purpose
Software fragpipe_dda_combined | fragpipe_dda_individual | diann | peaks_xpro | custom — selects the loader branch (custom = dictionary-driven via build_pep_all)
SampleSet Human-readable experiment name; used in the auto-generated report title
Subset Subset name; becomes a filename prefix and a subfolder under FolderResults/FolderFigures
FolderDocumentation Absolute (or render-time-cwd-relative) path to the folder containing AnnotationFile
AnnotationFile CSV name within FolderDocumentation
FolderData / FolderResults / FolderFigures Absolute (or render-time-cwd-relative) paths for cached pep_all input / csv+xlsx output / png output
PepAllSource Focused reports only (the seven 01–07 templates, via inst/rmarkdown/shared/setup.Rmd): how to obtain pep_all — "cached" (default; load <Subset>_pep_all.rda from FolderData), "rda" (load PepAllFile), or "build" (parse the raw search output via build_pep_all() and write the cache). The two 00_* all-in-one reports ignore this (they always build / load their own way).
PeptideSet / QuantFeature / QuantUnit / MinReplicates / NormMethod / ImputeMethod / StatMethod / BlockVar / FdrCutoff / Log2FcCutoff / MinDetectExclusive / TopNHeatmap / PermutationTest 06_quant_stats only: which peptides to analyse ("selected" = pep_short, or "all"), the matrix rows (Peptide default | Sequence | PeptideID | ProteinFirst) and columns (BioReplicate default | Sample | Condition), the filtering cut-off (default 2 units in ≥1 Condition), normalization (median default | quantile | cyclicloess | scale | none), imputation (none default | minprob | mindet), test (limma default | ttest), an optional limma::duplicateCorrelation blocking column, the significance cut-offs, the detection-count rule for condition-exclusive features, the heatmap feature count, and whether to run the PERMANOVA permutation test.
PeptideSet / PropertySet / MotifLength / TerminalPositions / ChargePh / MinPeptidesSample / FdrCutoff 07_pepchem only: which peptides to analyse ("selected" = pep_short, or "all"), the descriptor set (core = Length/GRAVY/pI/Charge | extended adds MW, Boman, hydrophobic moment, instability + aliphatic index and the frac_* class fractions — see pepchem_properties()), the peptide length used for the per-position frequency map ("auto" = modal length, or an integer), the comma-separated positions profiled across all lengths (negative counts from the C-terminus), the pH of the net-charge descriptor, the unique-sequence count below which a sample is flagged as noisy, and the BH significance cut-off.
Provider Organisation/person that produced the report, printed in the header via provider_line(). Default "" prints a generic attribution naming no organisation. Declared by all nine templates.
QCColumn / ThresholdMode 05_quality_score only: QCColumn is the annotation column flagging QC controls (default "QC"; empty disables QC tagging); ThresholdMode is "default" (literature thresholds) or "qc_relative" (calibrate from the QC samples).
PepAllFile Explicit .rda path, used only when PepAllSource = "rda"
Instrument tims_tof | faims_orbi | orbi — controls ion-mobility (1/k0) handling
MHCclass "MHC1" (human, 8–13 AA, default), "MHC1_mouse" (murine H-2, 7–11 AA) or "MHC2" (12–25 AA) — sets shortpep_range and the palette via mhc_length_window()/mhc_class_palette(); overrides ShortPeptideLengthMin/Max
ShortPeptideLengthMin/Max Custom pep_short window; used only when MHCclass is not a recognised value
ResultsOverwrite FALSE makes check_output_exists/check_file_exists abort if outputs already exist
TestMode TRUE = keep only the first ~100 rows per run (fast iteration on a representative subset — every run/Condition/replicate survives, unlike a head-of-file truncation of a combined export; can still break correlation plots)
CsvSave / PlotsSave TRUE = also export intermediary csvs / png plots

run_howmahico_report() always writes input_params.csv (package version + render timestamp + every param, long-format, via write_input_params()/write.csv_rawr()) into FolderResults, independent of CsvSave/PlotsSave — joining pep_all.csv, counts_pep_all_condition.csv, and seq_by_condition.xlsx in the “always written” export tier (see “Export tiers” below). The report header’s code-version line is now `r packageVersion("HowMaHiCo")` — reads from DESCRIPTION, can’t drift out of sync with a hand-typed string.

Dependencies are declared in DESCRIPTION (Imports/Suggests, per project-style-guide.md’s meta-package-free convention) rather than library()-ed at the top of a sourced script — deltaProtR is not one of them: the one function HowMaHiCo originally borrowed from it (get_dirs_index_peaks) now lives natively in R/loaders-peaks-dirs.R.

Conventions & gotchas

  • Software drives everything downstream — the loader branch in the Rmd’s “Loading files” chunk dispatches on this string (grepl("fragpipe_dda", ...), == "diann", == "peaks_xpro"). Valid combined-vs-individual mode is inferred from whether "combined"/"individual" appears in the Software string. The "custom" value is handled only in build_pep_all() (not the inline-parsing 00_* reports): it dispatches on the YAML dictionary instead of hard-coded loader logic.
  • FragPipe currently reads psm.tsv, not peptide-level results — this means FDR is applied only at the PSM level, not the peptide level (a warning() documents this explicitly in the template; treat FragPipe peptide counts with that caveat in mind).
  • DIA-NN: ppm is a hardcoded dummy (= 0) because DIA-NN doesn’t report a calculated m/z to derive mass error from. Mass itself is computed (from Precursor.Mz/Precursor.Charge via formula — not the calibrated/observed mass the other loaders use); the in-template warning() lumps both columns together as “missing… dummy”, which overstates the case for Mass — check diann_parse_pep_all directly if precision matters.
  • Instrument only changes loader behavior for PEAKS (read_pep_peaks): tims_tof parses the X1_k0_Range column directly into invk0; faims_orbi/orbi repurpose Compensation Voltage (CV) as a stand-in (“not fully supported yet” per inline comments/messages). The FragPipe (Ion_Mobility) and DIA-NN (IM) loaders map straight to invk0 regardless of Instrument.
  • Fixed — FolderFigures/FolderResult typos in the setup chunk (a copy-paste slip present in BOTH legacy Rmds, that would have sent ggsave_rawr PNG output into 3_results/<subset> instead of 4_figures/<subset>, and referenced the nonexistent params$FolderResult): 01_report_main_template.Rmd ~L86/L92/L98 was corrected first; 02_report_upsets.Rmd ~L78/L84/L90 had the same bug (FolderFigures <- params$FolderResults in both branches, check_output_exists(params$FolderResult, ...)) and was caught/fixed during the Phase-4 conversion. Both inst/rmarkdown/templates/*/skeleton/skeleton.Rmd now carry the corrected pattern.
  • Overwrite guards: check_file_exists / check_output_exists throw before rendering if target files already exist and ResultsOverwrite = FALSE — intentional, to prevent silently clobbering prior analysis runs.
  • Export tiers: pep_all.csv, counts_pep_all_condition.csv, and seq_by_condition.xlsx are always written; everything else (per-sample log2Area matrices, count summaries, upset tables, PNG plots) is gated behind CsvSave/PlotsSave.
  • Code version in the report header is `r packageVersion("HowMaHiCo")` — reads from DESCRIPTION automatically. When template logic changes meaningfully, bump DESCRIPTION’s Version: field, add a matching entry to NEWS.md (newest version first — pkgdown renders it as the Changelog), and update the “Current version” line at the top of this file.
  • For the longer-term packaging conventions (R package structure, Docker, Shiny app, CI/release process) this project is expected to follow once matured into a distributable tool, see project-style-guide.md.

Deferred designs

Work that was planned in detail, then parked. Kept here (rather than only as a one-line plans_dgz.md standby entry) so it can be resumed without re-deriving the investigation.

Peptide position within the parent protein (deferred v0.16.0)

The third part of the physicochemical-properties request. Out of scope of 07_pepchem because it is the only part needing user-supplied input beyond pep_all.

  • No loader carries a position column. FragPipe’s psm.tsv select() whitelist (R/loaders-fragpipe.R) drops Protein Start/Protein End; DIA-NN’s report.tsv has none at all (RT.Start/RT.Stop are retention time); PEAKS’ start/end live in protein-peptides.csv, which the package never reads. The software = "custom" dictionary path is the one place a Start column would survive today, since parse_unified() imposes no whitelist beyond the dictionary.
  • Approach when resumed: an optional FastaFile report param plus a ~25-line base-R FASTA reader (read_fasta() → Header, Accession, Sequence, ProteinLength; accession = field 2 of a sp|P01234|NAME header, else the first whitespace token) and map_peptide_positions(), joining ProteinFirst (first entry when ;-separated) to the FASTA and locating each peptide with stringr::str_locate(..., fixed(Sequence)) → Start, End, RelPosition, DistNterm, DistCterm, warning with the unmapped fraction. No new dependency. It would also unlock a true proteome background for the composition section, replacing the pooled-subset reference 07_pepchem currently uses.
  • Plot: plot_protein_position(pos, type = c("relative", "terminal")), in a results='asis' section that emits its own heading only when a FASTA is given (the imputation-section pattern in 06_quant_stats).
  • Test fixture needed: the shipped sim data has 462 peptides over synthetic accessions (sp|Q8R3TN|NM3_HUMAN …) with no real protein to locate them in. Generate inst/extdata/sim_fragpipe_dda_proteins.fasta — one ~150–250 AA synthetic protein per Protein ID, each embedding its peptide(s) at a random offset (~80 KB against the existing 532 KB fixture dir). Leave a few accessions out to exercise the unmapped-fraction warning.
